market_sizing.target_buyer: Winery owner / general manager / cellar-door manager at a small-to-mid producer (5k-200k cases/year). For larger wineries, the operations or DTC manager.
market_sizing.business_count_au: Approximately 2,000 wine producers in Australia (Wine Australia 'Sector at a Glance'). Roughly 1,400-1,600 of these operate a cellar door / DTC presence (Wine Australia DTC survey). 65 wine regions across all states; concentration in SA, VIC, NSW, WA, TAS.
market_sizing.business_count_global: Global TAM ~120,000-150,000 wineries: US ~11,500 (WI/WBM 2024); France ~85,000 (incl. small growers); Italy ~45,000; Spain ~4,300; NZ ~700; Canada ~700; UK ~1,000 (growing fast). Most TAM concentrated in old-world fragmentation.
market_sizing.typical_size: AU: 5-50 employees including seasonal vintage labour; AUD $500k-$20M revenue. Mode is a family-owned producer at <50k cases/yr.

pricing_reality.incumbent_pricing: vintrace 'Essentials' from USD $195/mo, 'Professional' from USD $345/mo; InnoVint from USD $129/mo entry (custom-quoted, typically USD $300-$1,200/mo for production size). Vinsight (NZ-built, AU-popular) is more SMB-friendly, typically NZD $100-$400/mo. VinNOW perpetual + low monthly. Ezy Systems, Cepaos and CitySoft (SAP Business One based) are mid-market AUD $500-$2,500/mo. POS-only (PBSA, Square for cellar door) AUD $50-150/mo per terminal. WineDirect/vinSUITE DTC platforms add USD $200-500/mo plus transaction fees.
pricing_reality.willingness_to_pay: AUD $150-$500/mo for a single integrated production + cellar-door + WET module at SMB tier; AUD $500-$1,500/mo for full operations + DTC + compliance at mid-market. AU pays ~75-85% of US willingness given Wine-Australia-specific value (WET, LRBA, Wine Australia label approvals).
pricing_reality.sales_motion: Inside sales + demo + free trial. Industry-event presence essential (Wine Industry IMPACT, vintage conferences). Founder-led for first 100 customers.
pricing_reality.expansion_revenue_potential: Strong. Embedded payments on DTC and wine-club (2.5-3.5% take), wine-club subscription fees, label-design marketplace, allocations & en primeur SaaS, freight/3PL integrations, Wine Australia label-approval automation, export compliance per-shipment fees, WET rebate automation as success fee. Realistic 2-3x ARPU expansion via DTC payments alone.

competitive_landscape.incumbents: vintrace (AU-founded, acquired by Encompass Technologies 2018, ~2,000 customers globally, strong AU/NZ base, dominant in mid-market production); InnoVint (US, SF-based, ~1,000 customers, US-centric, Series B 2021); Vinsight (NZ, SMB-friendly, popular in AU/NZ small wineries, has WET support); Ezy Systems (AU, on-prem heritage, mid-market AU); Cepaos (AU-built, newer, Wine Australia compliance focused); CitySoft/Solutions+ Wine One (SAP B1 reseller, large producers); WineDirect, vinSUITE, Commerce7 (DTC/club-focused, US-centric); Unleashed (AU/NZ inventory with WET workflow).
competitive_landscape.incumbent_age_years: vintrace ~17 years (founded 2008/2009); InnoVint ~10 years (founded 2014); Vinsight ~12 years; Ezy Systems 20+ years; WineDirect (now Bottlerocket Wine Distribution) ~20 years. Dominant incumbent vintrace is ~17 years old — replatform window is open and the encompasstech acquisition has slowed product velocity.
competitive_landscape.user_satisfaction_signals: Capterra/SoftwareAdvice reviews of vintrace: 'sparkling wine module is very problematic — cannot partially disgorge without splitting the tirage lot, introduces falsities into traceability'; 'vendor less responsive than they used to be, not open to feedback', 'helpdesk could be more interactive', 'interface daunting at first glance', 'too open-ended — trial and error to set up'. InnoVint praised for UX but criticised on price and US-bias (no native WET). General industry complaint: WET reporting still done in spreadsheets even with software in place; DTC, cellar-door POS, wine-club and production almost always separate stacks (vintrace + Commerce7 + Xero + Shopify is common). Forum threads cite double data entry between production and DTC as the biggest day-to-day pain.
competitive_landscape.recent_funding_or_ma: Encompass Technologies (owner of vintrace) consolidating beverage software portfolio. Commerce7 acquired by Vinney/Sandbox in 2024. No major AU-specific winery SaaS funding in 2025-2026. Wine industry tech M&A is more consolidation than greenfield. Australian Grape & Wine secured continued Wine Tourism & Cellar Door Grant funding (Sept 2025) — a positive demand signal but not a software funding event.
competitive_landscape.ai_disruption_risk: Low-to-moderate. A few AI-native wine startups (Tastry for consumer matching, Crush AI for fermentation analytics) but no AI-native production+DTC+compliance suite yet. Window remains open 18-36 months, especially for AU compliance focus.

opportunity_quality.core_pain: Wineries run 3-5 disconnected systems: production (vintrace/spreadsheets), cellar-door POS (Square/PBSA), wine-club + DTC eCom (Commerce7/Shopify/WineDirect), accounting (Xero/MYOB), and WET/Wine Australia compliance (Excel + ATO portal). Reconciling bottle counts from vintage through cellar door to shipped DTC is manual; WET rebate claims (29% to AUD $100k via Wine Tourism & Cellar Door Grant + producer rebate) require careful eligible-sales tracking; label approvals via Wine Australia Label Integrity Program done off-platform. The unsolved workflow is unified bottle-level inventory + WET + cellar-door CRM + wine-club allocations in one AU-localised SaaS.
opportunity_quality.moat_source: AU-specific WET / Wine Australia compliance automation (regulatory moat); integrations with Wine Australia Label Approval System and LRBA portal; Xero/MYOB deep integration; wine-club + allocations data network effects (members carry across vintages); Wine Tourism & Cellar Door Grant claim automation as success-fee revenue.
opportunity_quality.critical_integrations: Xero, MYOB, Square, Stripe, Tyro (AU EFTPOS), Shopify, Wine Australia portals (Label Approval System, LRBA, export certificates), ATO BAS / WET return, Australia Post / StarTrack / Sendle, Mailchimp/Klaviyo, Vinify / Wine Depot 3PLs, Tastings booking (Now Book It), bottle-supplier EDI.
opportunity_quality.incumbent_ehr_lock_in: Low. Wineries are not locked into a single 'EHR' — they cobble together best-of-breed. Replacement is feasible by leading with one module (cellar-door POS or WET compliance) and expanding.

build_difficulty.regulatory_complexity: Moderate-to-high. WET (29% of wholesale value) calculations, producer rebate (up to AUD $350k), Wine Tourism & Cellar Door Grant (up to AUD $100k), Wine Australia Label Integrity Program, export certificates, Wine Australia LRBA reporting, ATO BAS, liquor licensing per state, RSA. Not as heavy as healthcare but several rule engines required.
build_difficulty.regulatory_changes_2025_2026: Wine Tourism & Cellar Door Grant extended for 3 more years (announced Sept 2025) — confirms ongoing claim/reporting workflow. Wine Australia Label Integrity Program continues; container deposit scheme variations across states; possible WET reform discussions ongoing but no firm date. EU CSRD-style sustainability reporting starting to pressure exporters in 2026-2027. Australian Government's $51.3b sector economic-contribution report (Sept 2025) bolsters policy attention. No NSW-eCoC-style hard cliff date that forces churn.
build_difficulty.domain_depth: High. Vintage cycle, blend traceability (lot splits, additions, transfers), bottling runs, WET law nuance, wine-club allocations, en-primeur, and DTC compliance per shipping state require deep domain experience. Realistically needs a wine-industry advisor or co-founder. Steeper than dental lab.
build_difficulty.mvp_effort: 9-12 months for a credible MVP covering production + cellar-door POS + WET + Xero. Lighter (cellar-door + WET + wine club only) MVP in 6 months.
build_difficulty.technical_risks: Lot-splitting / blend traceability data model is non-trivial; bottle-level vs litre-level inventory across the production-DTC boundary; WET calculation edge cases; Wine Australia portal scraping (no public API for many functions); offline-tolerant cellar-door POS on iPad during vintage.
build_difficulty.state_by_state_variance_au: Moderate. Liquor licensing differs per state (NSW, VIC, SA, WA each have own regulator); container deposit schemes differ; DTC shipping rules mostly federal. Not as bad as building codes (NCC) but multiple rule sets required.
build_difficulty.data_residency_requirement: Soft. Wine Australia and ATO are AU-facing but no hard hosting mandate. AU region hosting expected by customers.

distribution_difficulty.channel_options: Wine Industry IMPACT conference, vintage conferences, regional wine association sponsorships (Barossa Grape & Wine, McLaren Vale, Hunter Valley, Margaret River, Yarra Valley etc.), Daily Wine News / WBM / Wine Business / Winetitles newsletters, partnerships with wine consultants, accountants specialising in WET, Xero advisor network, content/SEO on 'WET rebate calculator', cold outbound to wineries (publicly listed via Wine Australia, regional bodies).
distribution_difficulty.trade_association_count_au: 20+ active: Australian Grape & Wine (peak body), Wine Australia (govt), plus regional associations for each of the 65 wine regions. Big sponsorship surface.
distribution_difficulty.trade_publication_count: 5-7: Daily Wine News, WBM (Wine Business Magazine), Winetitles, Australian & New Zealand Grapegrower & Winemaker, The Drinks Association magazine, Drinks Trade. All sell sponsorship.
distribution_difficulty.conference_event_count_au: Many. Wine Industry IMPACT (national), Outlook Conference, regional vintage events, Wine Communicators of Australia events, plus the AWITC (biennial). At least 8-12 viable annual events; small booths achievable under $10k.
distribution_difficulty.cold_outbound_viability: High. Wineries are publicly listed by Wine Australia, regional bodies, and tourism boards. Email and phone discoverable. Founder names public.
distribution_difficulty.founder_market_fit_proxy: Moderate. The industry is welcoming to operations-savvy outsiders if they show vintage knowledge. Wine-family inheritance bias exists. Co-founder/advisor with vintage cred recommended.
distribution_difficulty.case_study_acquisition_cost: Achievable: 5 reference customers in 4-6 months by anchoring to a single regional association (e.g., McLaren Vale or Yarra Valley) and a sympathetic accountant partner.
distribution_difficulty.content_seo_competitiveness: Low-moderate for AU-specific terms ('WET rebate software', 'cellar door POS Australia', 'wine club software Australia'). vintrace/Vinsight dominate global terms but AU long-tail is winnable in 6-9 months.
distribution_difficulty.insurer_or_gatekeeper_dependency: Moderate. Wine Australia Label Approval System and LRBA have no public API; export certificate workflow goes through Wine Australia. Workable via screen-scraping/PDF generation; not a startup-blocking gate.

personal_fit.manuva_data_model_reuse_pct: ~45-55%. Reuse: production orders (vintage batches), BOM (additions, dosages, packaging), inventory (bulk wine in tanks, bottled stock, dry goods), suppliers, bin/location (tank/barrel/warehouse), activity log. New: lot-split lineage, blending math, wine-club & allocations, POS, WET module, label-approval workflow, customer CRM at scale.
personal_fit.manuva_code_reuse: Tenant, RLS, auth, server actions, design system, Supabase + Next.js 15 scaffolding. Activity log and bin-aisle uniqueness patterns relevant for tank/barrel locations. iPad POS will need new patterns.
personal_fit.buyer_persona_overlap_with_manuva: Low. Wine producers are not Manuva's current ICP. Some Manuva food/bev manufacturers may overlap, but largely fresh GTM.
personal_fit.adjacency_to_manufacturing: Medium. Production workflow (blends, batches, BOM, bin/tank locations) maps; DTC/cellar-door/wine-club is a new retail layer Manuva doesn't have.
personal_fit.technical_moat_durability_months: 12-18 months for core ops; 24+ months once WET automation, Wine Australia integrations, and wine-club data are entrenched.

unit_economics.gross_margin_sensitivity: Healthy with caveats. POS hardware (iPad/printer) is pass-through; payments are net-positive once embedded; AI inference (auto-blend math, label OCR) modest. SMS/email/marketing send costs need pass-through. Expect 75-82% gross margin at scale.
unit_economics.multi_location_natural: Yes for mid/large producers (multiple cellar doors, multiple wineries under one parent — Treasury Wine Estates etc.). Single-cellar-door wineries dominate the tail.
unit_economics.churn_risk: Moderate. Wineries occasionally fold or sell during downturns (current AU wine glut and 2025 oversupply increases churn risk among tail producers). High switching cost once compliance + wine-club are entrenched offsets this for survivors.
unit_economics.customers_needed_for_target_arr: ~250-330 customers at AUD $3-4k ARR for AUD $1M ARR domestically; could be hit with ~20% AU winery share — realistic but requires multi-year grind.
